games.reason: A has the clearer allelic-binding prediction: its single passing REL-family model predicts stronger binding to alt (E13), while the AT-hook family’s two passing models disagree on direction despite a positive aggregate effect (E15). The occupancy evidence does not otherwise distinguish them: RELA and HMGA1 both lack a HepG2 peak at the variant (E25, E27), and neither chain has expression support. Their element, gene, cell-type, and phenotype links are similarly unestablished.

Both chains lack expression context and have a tested-negative HepG2 ChIP result for the TF associated with the screened model (E25, E27), so those findings do not distinguish them. The allele-specific prediction favors B: its RELA-mapped model predicts stronger alt binding without a reported direction conflict, whereas the F3 models disagree on direction despite the aggregate alt-favoring result. Thus the binding evidence is more direct and internally consistent for B.
